authority: BCH Cloak's sole authority for named route selection, agent kind, model, reasoning effort, and route-selection criteria. Launchers must consume this file; prose may name routes but must not copy their kind, model, or effort values. Environment, persona, account, memory integration, and other launch plumbing are outside that authority.

chore.use: Mechanical, isolated work such as renames, documentation alignment, evidence bookkeeping, generated-file refreshes, and report formatting.

engineer.use: Default implementation route for a narrow, well-understood engineering slice.

engineer-xhigh.use: Cross-package, concurrent, protocol, parity, or otherwise difficult implementation work.

engineer-max.use: Exceptional implementation only after a measured repeated failure or for unusually difficult correctness-critical logic; never a default.

engineer-opus.use: Implementation on the Claude pool when the operator names Opus as the engineer for a workstream; same scope rules as engineer.

engineer-opus-xhigh.use: Cross-package, protocol, parity, or otherwise difficult implementation on the Claude pool when the operator names Opus as the engineer for a workstream.

engineer-opus-max.use: Escalation implementation on the Claude pool only after measured repeated failure (two failed fix rounds or a failed escalation) and with the operator naming Opus at max; never a default.

engineer-astra.use: Implementation on the Codex pool when the operator names Astra as the engineer for a workstream (operator 2026-09-27, Claude quota low); same scope rules as engineer. A Daybreak cyber refusal gets one neutral re-prompt, then engineer-xhigh.

review.use: Ordinary independent exact-commit review of a bounded change with strong deterministic tests.

review-critical.use: Independent review involving privacy, cryptography, semantics, trust, recovery, lifecycle, package boundaries, frozen artifacts, proving, live-chain behavior, broad cross-package effects, or adversarial negative controls.

review-opus.use: Ordinary independent review on the Claude pool when that pool is available.

review-critical-opus.use: Critical independent review on the Claude pool when that pool is available.

review-critical-astra.use: First critical review of a custody or cryptography slice engineered on engineer-astra, when the operator routes reviews to Astra; falls back to review-critical if a Daybreak cyber check stops it.

review-escalate.use: Escalation only after two stuck review/fix rounds on the same finding, or when the remaining issue is an unexplained result; never a first review.

review-escalate-claude.use: Claude-pool escalation only after two stuck review/fix rounds on the same finding; never a first review.

research-opus-max.use: Operator-requested design research on an open protocol problem with no known approach; produces a proposal for review, never an implementation.

research-astra-max.use: Operator-requested design research on an open protocol problem with no known approach; produces a proposal for review, never an implementation.

research-sol-max.use: Operator-requested design research on an open protocol problem with no known approach; produces a proposal for review, never an implementation.

unblock.use: Research an unexplained result, clarify genuinely unknown scope, or find an unblocker that is not already known.

settle.use: Default fresh orchestrator that settles a finished run with a clean independent review and coherent evidence.

settle-critical.use: Settlement involving conflicting evidence, consequential acceptance, or unresolved semantic or security judgment.

executive.use: Fresh short-lived orchestrator for routine queue progression and dispatch decisions.

monitor.use: One-shot read-only status from concise durable evidence; no acceptance, dispatch, repeated waits, or implementation.

rules: Select by task class, not ad hoc per item. The route table below is the whole policy.
The reviewer always runs on the other provider from the engineer (independence and load balance). Settles and routine orchestration stay on Codex.
Opus trips its own cyber safeguard on adversarial, covert-channel and custody-attack work: those classes go to Codex whichever pool is primary.
Tier equivalence: Opus high = Sol high; Opus xhigh = Sol xhigh; escalation frontier = Fable (Claude) or Astra (Codex).
Pool switch: when one provider's weekly quota is the tighter one, the operator flips primary_implementation_pool; the cross-provider review rule does not change.
Balance is measured, not assumed: .lane/supervisor/tidy-tabs.sh prints runs per provider and effort for the last 24 hours.
